items.description: A gateway (System → Gateways → Configuration). For WireGuard site-to-site, point it at the remote peer's tunnel address on the assigned WireGuard interface, and use it in opnsense_route.

name.description: Gateway name; static routes refer to it.

interface.description: Assigned interface name, e.g. `opt3` (Interfaces → Assignments), not the device name `wg0`.

gateway.description: Gateway IP, e.g. the remote peer's tunnel address. Empty means dynamic.

defaultgw.description: Use as the default (upstream) gateway. Leave false for a VPN peer.

fargw.description: Allow a gateway outside the interface's subnet. Needed when the WireGuard instance has a /32 tunnel address.

monitor_disable.description: Monitor the gateway with dpinger (shows loss/latency, enables failover).

monitor.description: Address to ping when monitoring; defaults to the gateway address.

priority.description: Lower wins when several gateways could be the default.

items.description: A static route (System → Routes → Configuration): send a destination network to a gateway.

network.description: Destination network in CIDR notation, e.g. `192.168.50.0/24`.

gateway.description: Gateway *name*, e.g. `opnsense_gateway.site2.name`. Static routes reference gateways by name, so referencing the resource also orders creation correctly.

items.description: A gateway group (System → Gateways → Groups): failover and load balancing. Gateways in the same tier share the load; a higher tier is used when everything in the lower tiers is down. Use the group name as the gateway of a firewall rule or route.

item.description: Gateways in tier 1 (preferred; several share the load).

item2.description: Gateways in tier 2; used when every tier below it is down.

item3.description: Gateways in tier 3; used when every tier below it is down.

item4.description: Gateways in tier 4; used when every tier below it is down.

item5.description: Gateways in tier 5; used when every tier below it is down.

trigger.description: When a member counts as down: `down`, `downloss` (packet loss), `downlatency` or `downlosslatency`.

poolopts.description: Load-balancing mode within a tier; empty for the default.
